title: Review: Organisation of an ecosystem; Biodiversity and the effect of human interaction
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for AQA GCSE Biology (8461) (status of the source: authored-gated-unreviewed). Terms and clues: 4.7.2-c01 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.7.2-c07 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.7.2-c15 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.7.2-c08 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition. Questions: 4.7.2-q04, 4.7.2-q07, 4.7.2-q08, 4.7.3-q02, 4.7.3-q03, 4.7.3-q05, 4.7.3-q06, 4.7.3-q07, 4.7.3-q08, 4.7.2-q05, 4.7.2-x01 (written for the game), 4.7.2-q10. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Producer
items.clue: The organism at the start of a food chain, which synthesises molecules.

items.label: Transect
items.clue: A line marked across a habitat, along which quadrats are placed at intervals.

items.label: Compost
items.clue: The material produced when gardeners and farmers provide optimum conditions for rapid decay of waste biological material.

items.label: Arithmetic mean
items.clue: The total of all the readings divided by the number of readings, used to summarise the abundance of a species from repeated quadrat counts.

questions.stem: A student places five quadrats at random in a field and counts the daisies in each: 7, 0, 6, 7, 5. What is the mean number of daisies per quadrat?

options.text: 6.0 daisies per quadrat
7.0 daisies per quadrat
5.0 daisies per quadrat
6.25 daisies per quadrat

questions.explanation: The arithmetic mean is the total of the readings divided by the number of readings: 25 daisies divided by 5 quadrats gives 5.0 daisies per quadrat.

questions.stem: Which statement describes how the water cycle provides fresh water for plants and animals on land?

options.text: Salt water drains from the seas onto the land
Water used up by organisms is lost from the land
Water is continuously evaporated and precipitated
Water is lost to the seas and is not returned

questions.explanation: The water cycle provides fresh water for plants and animals on land before draining into the seas, because water is continuously evaporated and precipitated.

questions.stem: A gardener wants rapid decay of waste plant material in a compost heap, to use the compost as a natural fertiliser. Which conditions give the fastest rate of decay?

options.text: Very hot, dry, with oxygen present
Warm, moist and with oxygen present
Warm, moist and with oxygen kept out
Warm, dry and with oxygen present

questions.explanation: Temperature, water and the availability of oxygen affect the rate of decay, so gardeners provide optimum conditions: warm, moist and with oxygen available.

questions.stem: A woodland has a great biodiversity. Why is this ecosystem more stable?

options.text: The number of individual organisms stays the same
Each species depends more on others for shelter
One species depends less on others for its food
The area contains a larger number of habitats

questions.explanation: A great biodiversity ensures the stability of ecosystems by reducing the dependence of one species on another for food, shelter and the maintenance of the physical environment.

questions.stem: As the human population grows, more untreated sewage and fertiliser drain into a river and many fish and plants die. What is the effect on the river?

options.text: There is no pollution as both are natural materials
Pollution kills organisms and biodiversity falls
Biodiversity is unchanged as fish numbers recover
Biodiversity falls but the ecosystem becomes stable

questions.explanation: More waste is produced as the population grows, and unless it is properly handled more pollution is caused; pollution kills plants and animals which can reduce biodiversity.

questions.stem: A peat bog is drained and the peat is dug out and sold as garden compost. What are the effects?

options.text: The habitat is lost and carbon dioxide is released
Carbon dioxide is released by burning, not by decay
Biodiversity is unchanged as many organisms survive
The land stays available because it is not built on

questions.explanation: The destruction of peat bogs to produce garden compost reduces the area of this habitat, and thus its biodiversity, and the decay or burning of the peat releases carbon dioxide into the atmosphere.

questions.stem: A large area of tropical forest is cleared to grow crops for biofuels. What is the impact on biodiversity?

options.text: Biodiversity is unchanged because biofuels are renewable
Biodiversity falls when the cleared trees are burned
Biodiversity falls as the forest habitat is destroyed
Biodiversity falls, so the ecosystem becomes more stable

questions.explanation: Large-scale deforestation in tropical areas, including clearance to grow crops for biofuels, removes the habitat and so reduces the variety of species living there.

questions.stem: Levels of carbon dioxide and methane in the atmosphere are increasing. Which is a biological consequence of the global warming this causes?

options.text: Species die out where the air becomes much warmer
Some species change the areas where they are found
Areas near carbon dioxide sources are affected most
Ecosystems become more stable as species are lost

questions.explanation: Biological consequences of global warming include loss of habitat, changes in the distribution of species and changes in migration patterns.

questions.stem: A government wants to reduce the negative effects of humans on ecosystems and biodiversity. Which policy would have a positive impact?

options.text: Growing more crops that will be used to make biofuels
Spreading extra fertiliser on farmland each season
Digging up more peat bogs to sell as garden compost
Reducing deforestation and carbon dioxide emissions

questions.explanation: Reduction of deforestation and of carbon dioxide emissions by some governments is one of the programmes put in place to reduce the negative effects of humans on ecosystems and biodiversity.

questions.stem: Counts of daisies per quadrat range from 2 to 46. Which scale should the student use on the y-axis when plotting these results?

options.text: 0 to 50, using steps of 2, 5, 10
0 to 50, using equal steps of 5
0 to 500, using equal steps of 50
2 to 46, using steps of 4 then 10

questions.explanation: An appropriate scale goes up in equal steps and lets the range of the data fill most of the grid, so all counts from 2 to 46 can be plotted accurately.

questions.stem: In the carbon cycle, which process removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere?

options.text: Respiration in plants
Decay by microorganisms
Photosynthesis in plants
Burning fossil fuels

questions.explanation: Plants take in carbon dioxide for photosynthesis; respiration, decay and combustion all release it.

questions.stem: Why must a biogas generator be sealed so that air cannot get in?

options.text: Methane is produced by anaerobic decay
Methane is produced faster in warmer air
Oxygen is needed to produce the methane
Bacteria need air to produce the methane

questions.explanation: Anaerobic decay produces methane gas, so a biogas generator is sealed to keep oxygen out and produce methane gas that can be used as a fuel.
